# Project files the editor leaves to you

The Pix3 editor edits a project that is already open: nodes, properties, what is inside a
prefab, the clips of a `.pix3anim`, the entries of a locale table. It **never creates, renames,
moves or deletes a file, never edits `pix3project.yaml` and never builds**. When the human asks
for one of those, you do it — by writing files and running the CLI. The editor follows the disk
on its own. After every recipe: `pix3 check`, then (editor open) `pix3_sync` with `expect` =
the sha256 of every file you wrote, or (no editor) `pix3 smoke <the scene>`.

| The human asks for | Recipe |
| --- | --- |
| a new scene, a copy of a scene ("Save As") | [New scene](#new-scene) |
| a folder | create it; the asset panel shows it |
| a script | `export class X extends Script` in `scripts/X.ts` — `pix3-scripts` |
| an asset renamed, moved or deleted | [Rename, move, delete](#rename-move-delete) |
| a branch of a scene turned into a prefab ("Save Branch as Prefab") | [Extract a branch into a prefab](#extract-a-branch-into-a-prefab) |
| a flipbook for an `AnimatedSprite2D` | `pix3anim.md` → "Create one and bind it" |
| a language added or removed | [Add or remove a locale](#add-or-remove-a-locale) |
| project settings (resolution, entry scene, quality, fonts …) | [`pix3project.yaml`](#pix3projectyaml) |
| a build, an export | `npm run build` → `dist/` — [Build options](#build-options) |
| an image | write an SVG (AGENTS.md rule 5), or the human generates one in the editor's Generate panel and saves it into the project |

## New scene

1. Copy the entry scene (`defaultExportScenePath` in `pix3project.yaml`) to
   `scenes/<name>.pix3scene` — it carries the root sized from `viewportBaseSize`. Keep the root
   and what every screen has (a background), drop the root's `components` and the children that
   are the other scene's game, and update `metadata.description` and the header comment. Ids
   only have to be unique **within** a scene, so a copy keeps them.
2. A scene under `scenes/` that is not under `scenes/prefabs/`, `prefabs/` or `scenes/ui/` is a
   playable scene: reach it with `await this.scene.changeScene('res://scenes/<name>.pix3scene')`.
   To make the game boot into it, set `defaultExportScenePath: scenes/<name>.pix3scene` — and
   give it a way on (a menu's button script calls `changeScene` to the game).
3. Under `scenes/prefabs/`, `prefabs/` or `scenes/ui/` the file is a prefab or an overlay: it is
   instanced, never booted.

## Rename, move, delete

Everything refers to files by path, and nothing rewrites those paths for you.

1. Find every reference first, in every text file of the project (not `node_modules/`,
   `.pix3/`, `dist/`, `.git/`, and not the kit's own docs in `.claude/`):
   `grep -rn "sprites/coin.png" --exclude-dir={node_modules,.pix3,dist,.git,.claude} .` — for
   a folder, search it with its trailing slash (`sprites/coin/`), which `sprites/coins/` does
   not match.
   — scenes and prefabs (`res://…`), `.pix3anim` frame paths, `locales/*.json` `sprites`,
   scripts, and `pix3project.yaml` (which writes paths **without** `res://`:
   `defaultExportScenePath`, `fonts[].path`). Search the folder name too: a path a script builds
   at runtime (`` `res://levels/${n}.pix3scene` ``) has no literal to find.
2. Move the file (`git mv` when git tracks it, else `mv`) and rewrite every reference; a folder
   move rewrites the prefix. A flipbook folder keeps its `<name>/<name>.pix3anim` pairing:
   renaming `sprites/coin/` to `sprites/coins/` renames `coin.pix3anim` to `coins.pix3anim` too.
   To delete, first remove or replace the references, then the file.
3. `pix3 check` names a scene reference that still points nowhere (`E_MISSING_RESOURCE`,
   `E_MISSING_PREFAB`); it does not look inside `.pix3anim` or locale files — `pix3 smoke` on a
   scene that uses them reports a missing file when it loads, as the **warning**
   `W_SMOKE_MISSING_RESOURCE` (exit 0).

A script's file name is free to change: `type: user:Mover` names the exported class. Renaming
the class means rewriting every `type: user:Mover` and every `import`.

## Extract a branch into a prefab

The branch: a node of the host scene with everything under it, e.g. in `scenes/main.pix3scene`

```yaml
      - id: coin-hud
        type: Group2D
        name: Coin HUD
        properties:
          width: 260
          height: 80
          transform: { position: [0, 0], scale: [1, 1], rotation: 0 }
          layout: { enabled: true, horizontalAlign: left, verticalAlign: top, left: 60, top: 40 }
        children:
          - id: coin-icon
            type: ColorRect2D
            name: Coin Icon
            properties: { width: 64, height: 64, color: "#f5c542", transform: { position: [-80, 0] } }
          - id: coin-count
            type: Label2D
            name: Coin Count
            properties: { label: "0", labelFontSize: 48, transform: { position: [40, 0] } }
```

1. Sync and re-read the host scene (AGENTS.md rule 2).
2. Write `scenes/prefabs/CoinHud.pix3scene`: `version: 1.0.0` and a `root:` with **exactly one**
   node — the branch root, cut with everything under it (`properties`, `components`, `groups`,
   `children`) and indented back to the top level.
3. The prefab root keeps its size but not its placement: set its `transform` to
   `{ position: [0, 0], scale: [1, 1], rotation: 0 }` and drop its `layout:` block. Where it
   sits is the instance's business (step 5).
4. Ids. Keep the branch's ids — the prefab root's `id` as it was, the inner ones unique in the
   file. In the host scene the instance node's id becomes the root's id, and every inner node
   keeps its prefab id **when that id is free in the host scene**; otherwise the loader renames
   it `<id>-1`, `<id>-2`, … — which is what happens to the second instance of the same prefab.
   So a lookup by id (`findNode('coin-count')`) finds the first instance's node only; to reach
   an inner node of each instance, go through the instance — a second copy is one more instance
   node with an id and name you choose (`coin-hud-2`, "Coin HUD 2"), its inner `coin-count`
   becomes `coin-count-1`: `this.findNode('coin-hud-2')?.findByName('Coin Count')` (names never
   change; the renamed id is its `nodeId`). A `node` property of a component inside the prefab that names another
   node of the prefab is re-pointed per instance by the loader.
5. Replace the branch in the host scene, at the same place in `children` (tree order is paint
   order), with one instance node: the branch root's `id` (scripts that find it keep finding
   it) and `name`, `instance: res://scenes/prefabs/CoinHud.pix3scene`, and `properties` with the
   root's `transform` and its anchoring in the **flat** names an instance reads —
   `layoutEnabled`, `horizontalAlign`, `verticalAlign` and the margins `layoutLeft` /
   `layoutRight` / `layoutTop` / `layoutBottom` (scene-format "Prefab instance"). No `type`,
   no `components`, no `children`:

   ```yaml
      - id: coin-hud
        name: Coin HUD
        instance: res://scenes/prefabs/CoinHud.pix3scene
        properties:
          transform: { position: [0, 0] }
          layoutEnabled: true
          horizontalAlign: left
          verticalAlign: top
          layoutLeft: 60
          layoutTop: 40
   ```

6. A value that differed per copy goes into the instance: on the root as above, on an inner
   node in `overrides.byLocalId` (`coin-count: { properties: { label: "10" } }`, keyed by the
   prefab's ids). These are node **properties** and the values a copy starts with: a script
   inside the prefab that sets the same property in `onStart` wins, and a component's `config`
   cannot differ per copy (no component overrides) — make the script read the node property,
   or keep the tunable on a plain node of the host scene. Components start parent first, so a
   host script's `onStart` sees an inner node before the prefab's own scripts touched it. A
   label with a `labelKey` shows that key's text, whatever `label` says: per copy, override the
   `labelKey` (one key per copy) instead.
7. `pix3 check` — `E_PREFAB_ROOT` (not one root), `E_DUPLICATE_ID`, `E_MISSING_PREFAB`,
   `E_UNKNOWN_OVERRIDE_TARGET` name the slips — then sync with `expect` of both files and look
   at it running.

## Add or remove a locale

A locale is a table `locales/<id>.json` at the project root — `strings` (key → text, `{name}`
placeholders) and `sprites` (key → `res://` image for art with baked-in text). Nodes and
scripts name **keys** (`labelKey` on a UI control, `textureKey` on a `Sprite2D`,
`this.scene.localization.tr('menu.play')`), never a locale.

```json
{
  "$meta": { "locale": "de", "name": "Deutsch" },
  "strings": { "menu.play": "Spielen" },
  "sprites": {}
}
```

Add one:

0. No table yet: write the default one first — `locales/en.json` with the keys the game uses
   (`labelKey` on the nodes; keep `label` as well, it is what shows while there is no table) —
   and declare it alone (`locales: [en]`, step 2).
1. Copy the default locale's table to `locales/<id>.json`, set `$meta.locale` and `$meta.name`
   (`"direction": "rtl"` for a right-to-left language) and translate the values. Keep every key;
   one you cannot translate yet stays `""` and falls back to the fallback locale, then to the key.
2. Declare it in `pix3project.yaml`, creating the block if there is none:

   ```yaml
   localization:
     defaultLocale: en
     locales: [en, de]
   ```

   Without a block every `locales/*.json` is a locale (`en` the default when there is one);
   with it, only the tables it names count — the build ships those and no other.

Remove one:

1. Never the `defaultLocale` or the `fallbackLocale` — point those at another locale first.
2. Drop the id from `localization.locales`, delete `locales/<id>.json`, and grep the scripts for
   the id (`setLocale('de')`). An image only that table's `sprites` used is now unreferenced
   (`pix3 check` lists those under `sprites/` as `W_UNUSED_ASSET`).

Nothing checks the tables: a `labelKey` no table has shows the key itself on screen, and a
declared locale without its file loads empty — read the keys back yourself (or look at the
running game). In a script, `this.scene.localization`: `tr(key, { name: value })` (fills
`{name}`), `trPlural(key, count)`, `trSprite(key)`, `has(key)`, `locale`, `locales`,
`setLocale(id)`, `onChange(fn)`; a node shows `tr(node.labelKey)` when it has a key.

## `pix3project.yaml`

The manifest. Change a key only when the human asks for that setting (or a recipe above says
so), keep every key you do not know, and copy the style of the file.

| Key | What |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | `1.0.0`; leave it |
| `defaultExportScenePath` | the scene the game boots into (no `res://`) |
| `viewportBaseSize` | `{ width, height }` — the design resolution 2D layout is authored against |
| `projectType` | `2d` or `3d` |
| `targetPlatform` | `mobile`, `desktop` or `universal` |
| `textureFiltering` | `linear` (smooth) or `nearest` (pixel art) for 2D textures |
| `ambientOcclusion` | `off`, `baked`, `realtime` or `adaptive` — the project default |
| `quality` | `{ antialias, shadows, maxPixelRatio }` |
| `localization` | `{ defaultLocale, fallbackLocale?, locales }` — above |
| `fonts` | `[{ family, path, weight, style, unicodeRange? }]` — font files registered before the first frame; `path` without `res://` |
| `autoloads` | leave it `[]`: autoloads run only in the editor's play mode, never in `npm run dev` or a build. A script that must live for the whole game goes on the entry scene's root node |
| `metadata` | the editor's and `pix3 kit`'s bookkeeping (`projectId`, `agentKit`) — do not edit |

## Build options

`npm run build` writes `dist/index.html` (one self-contained file) and
`dist/<name>.report.json` (what it weighs and why). How it builds is `pix3()` in
`vite.config.ts`, not the manifest: `pix3({ build: 'zip' })` (a zip to host instead of one
file), `pix3({ compress: true })` (gzip inside the page, about two thirds smaller),
`pix3({ entryScene: 'scenes/level-1.pix3scene' })` (boot another scene than
`defaultExportScenePath`), `pix3({ strip: { keep: [...] } })` (when the build says a library
needs runtime classes it cannot see).
